## About me

![](profile.jpg){.about-avatar fig-alt="Risheekkumar Baskaran"}

I'm Risheekkumar Baskaran, a Senior Data Scientist at American Express, based in Chennai, India. My background spans data analytics and machine learning, with a focus on finding useful, actionable signals in complex data.

I build production machine learning systems across fraud, risk, marketing, and recommendations. My recent work includes pre-training a foundation transformer on 60 billion transactions, large-scale retrieval and ranking systems, and GenAI applications built with DSPy and GEPA. I care about models that work beyond a notebook: sound evaluation, efficient training, reliable inference, and measurable outcomes.

I also build open-source tools. [fastpragma](https://github.com/risheekkumarb/fastpragma) turns the PRAGMA architecture into a practical workflow for tokenizing event data, packing variable-length sequences, pre-training, and fine-tuning. Outside work, I enjoy playing chess and writing about systems I want to understand from first principles.

## About this blog

This blog is my working notebook for machine learning systems that I want to understand deeply. I write implementation-driven guides on foundation models, vector search, prompt optimization, recommender systems, cryptography, and the engineering choices that turn an idea into a working system.

The goal is simple: explain what I learned clearly enough that someone else can build on it. The [Archive](archive.qmd) contains all long-form articles, while [Projects](projects.qmd) collects the open-source work behind them.
